extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and intellectual property office examiners in ASEAN Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/procedural standards for filing, formalities examination, substantive requirements, and related procedural topics for patent applications across ASEAN Member States (AMS). Intended to guide applicants, agents and IPO examiners on required documents, timelines, fees, amendments, unity, divisional practice, translations, and related formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must file their patent application, including the specification, in the official language of the country of filing (for Cambodia, Lao PDR, Indonesia, Thailand and Viet Nam) and English (for Brunei Darussalam and Singapore). In Malaysia, Myanmar and the Philippines, applicants can choose between the official language of the country of filing and English. The language in which the patent is filed is also used as the language of the proceedings, and any amendments made to the application, or the patent must be drawn up in that language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in any language other than an official/authorized language, a translation of the specification (title, abstract, claims, description and drawings) in the required language must be filed within a specified period or upon request of the patent office/registrar. Note: in Myanmar, even if English is selected the proceedings of office communication are in the country’s official language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and information required for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must include: (1) Request for grant of a patent (application form) on prescribed form with official fee; (2) Title of the invention; (3) Abstract; (4) Description; (5) Claims; (6) Drawings (if any); (7) Priority (if applicable); (8) Power of Attorney (if applicant not resident); (9) Assignment/statement of inventorship/declaration of invention (if ownership transferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must specify technical field, indicate background art known to applicant useful for understanding/search, disclose the invention clearly and in sufficient detail to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it out, disclose at least one mode of making/using the invention, and briefly describe figures/drawings. Claims must be clear, supported by the description, define subject-matter in terms of technical features (structural/functional, including mathematical terms), and must not rely on references to description/drawings for technical features unless necessary to understand or improve clarity/conciseness. Request form must indicate minimum information (date, applicant details; inventor details may be required). Some AMS require name/address of resident agent and signature. Assignment/deed forms may be compulsory in some AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for translation, certification, notarization or legalization
rubrics_metrics.description: If specification is filed in a language other than the official/authorized language, a translation into an official language or other authorized language must be filed within a specified period or upon request. For priority documents, a certified copy of the priority application must be filed (exception: Singapore). If a power of attorney is signed abroad, it must be notarized or certified where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cambodia, Lao PDR and Thailand require notarization or national certification of POA; Cambodia, Lao PDR and the Philippines also require notarization of deed of assignment. National provisions specify exact periods and form/format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for late filing of documents and maximum deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS provide options for late filing of certain documents to permit expeditious filing of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In Singapore, applicants may submit claims within 12 months of the priority date (similar to provisional filing). Priority certified copy/translation, power of attorney, and assignment/statement may often be filed after initial filing within periods prescribed by national provisions or upon request of the office/registrar. Exact time limits and conditions vary by AMS and are described in national provisions/CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of specification for PCT national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For PCT National Phase applications in Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Viet Nam, the translation of the specification into an official language of the country of filing or other authorized language can be submitted after filing within the period prescribed in the respective national provisions, if applicable, upon request of the office/Registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to national provisions for precise deadlines and accepted languages. Some offices may require translation upon office request rather than at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim rules and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A national application may claim priority of an earlier application filed not more than 12 months before the filing date in a Paris Convention or WTO member state. The 12-month period is not extendable. Multiple priorities may be claimed in one national application. The effective date for novelty and inventive step is the priority date of the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants claiming priority must file a declaration of priority and provide a certified copy of the previous application (if applicable) and translations if necessary (note Singapore exception: provided only if requested). If the earlier application is not actually the first application by the applicant, the priority claim is invalid for subject-matter already disclosed in the still-earlier application. If a priority claim is made outside the 12-month period it is considered invalid and the local filing date becomes effective. Multiple priorities allocate the earliest priority date disclosed for each subject-matter portion. Fees may apply per priority claim in some AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of filing fees per application/claim/page and excess claims/pages fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from Thailand (fee per application irrespective of pages/claims), AMS generally calculate official filing fees by taking into account the number of claims and in some cases number of pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds for excess claims fee vary between 5 claims (Philippines) and 25 claims (Brunei); Viet Nam applies excess claim fee to independent claims only. Excess claims fees must be paid at filing (Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Philippines), at search/grant (Singapore), or at grant (Brunei, Viet Nam). Some AMS (Indonesia, Philippines, Viet Nam) also apply excess page fees with thresholds (e.g., pages in excess of five (Viet Nam) to thirty (Indonesia, Philippines)). See CSR Section 1.7 for calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and online payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Most AMS use web-based filing; some offer both e-filing and paper filing. Certain documents (e.g., original certified copy of foreign application for priority) may still need original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-filing systems often allow payment online via credit card, bank transfer or other providers. E-filing is intended to speed filing and support publication. Some AMS require electronic-only submission for certain filings (e.g., Indonesia and Singapore: only electronic submission acceptable for the request form; Singapore allows only electronic amendments). The CSR lists country-specific e-filing links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent and utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent or utility model (petty patent/simple patent/utility innovation) can be applied for based on a patent priority claim and vice versa in all AMS (exceptions: Brunei and Singapore, which have no utility model protection). Requests to convert a patent into a utility model or vice versa can be applied by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most AMS requests can be filed at any time before grant or refusal. Requirements vary by AMS; conversion cannot result in subject-matter beyond the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for pre-filing disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS operate a grace period such that if an applicant files within that period after disclosing the invention, specific earlier disclosures are not considered prior art for the patent application. Grace periods vary between AMS, ranging from six to twelve months, with most AMS providing twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace periods typically apply to disclosures by the inventor/applicant or their predecessors in title and may exempt disclosures made by abuse (e.g., breach of confidence). Some AMS (Philippines, Singapore, Viet Nam) cover disclosures made by the patent office (e.g., published in error). International exhibitions may be covered; certificate of disclosure at the exhibition may be required. If a prior abstract lacks enabling disclosure a patent may still be valid; inventive step must be assessed during substantive examination. A declaration of non-prejudicial disclosure may include type, date, title, place of disclosure. Evidence requirements (statutory declarations, affidavits) vary (Singapore requires evidence for printed publications by same authors; Viet Nam exception noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination — scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent applications undergo a formalities examination in-house before substantive examination. The formalities examination checks compliance with formal requirements and results in acceptance for further examination, acceptance subject to amendment(s), or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities examination typically requires identifying presence of request form, applicant/inventor identification, title, description, claims, drawings (if necessary), abstract, representative details, and priority claim. The contents of abstract, description, drawings, title and claims are not closely scrutinized in formalities per se; it is sufficient that documents identifiable as description and claims exist. However, some AMS perform initial checks on clarity, multiple dependency, claim(s) evaluation for priority (Philippines), exclusions/exception to patentability and initial clarity (Thailand), and unity 'a priori' in some cases. Supporting documents may be filed within prescribed periods after filing; extensions may be allowed per national provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection during formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner identifies deficiencies and invites remedy within a defined (possibly extendable) period; failure to remedy can lead to abandonment or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for abandonment/rejection include: required filing documents missing/erroneous/incomplete/non-compliant with format; missing title, abstract, description and/or claim(s); specification not translated timely into official language; foreign applicants not represented by professional representative where required; inventor designation not made or deed of assignment not submitted; filing/supporting documents not filed in due time; prescribed fees not paid on time; non-patentable subject matters (Thailand, Viet Nam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment before and during formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may, of their own initiative or at the request of the patent office/registrar, amend or correct the application including the specification without impacting the filing date, subject to procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be requested in the prescribed manner, within prescribed periods, and accompanied by prescribed documents/fees if applicable. Amendments accepted are entered in the application and considered for publication. New matter extending beyond the original disclosure will be rejected. There is no restriction on broadening claims as long as the amendment does not include matter extending beyond the originally filed disclosure; substantive examination will inform applicant if amendments constitute new matter and allow amendment within a prescribed time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after completion of formalities (pre-grant) — limits
rubrics_metrics.description: After completion of formalities examination, applicants may request amendment of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-grant amendments must not result in inclusion of subject-matter extending beyond that disclosed in the application as originally filed. National provisions govern how and when such amendments may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic or paper-based filing of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments can be filed electronically or on paper in most AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Singapore only allows amendments filed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. Assessment uses both a priori and a posteriori approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link between group must be a technical relationship expressed in the claims in terms of same or corresponding special technical features. Lack of unity must be determined from the language of the claims as properly construed and, where appropriate, by regard to relevant prior art. Unity may be lacking a priori (from claim language) or a posteriori (after considering prior art). Example: independent claims to A+Z, A+Y, Z+Y lack unity a priori absent common subject-matter to all three; A+Z and A+Y have unity a priori since A is common, but if A is found to be prior art after search, lack of unity a posteriori can arise. Assessment best during substantive examination but should be considered early to avoid unnecessary costs. Lack of unity should not be raised/maintained based on narrow or literal approach; adopt broad, practical consideration of interdependence of alternatives in relation to state of the art. Assessment should ensure efficient use of examination resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If unity of invention is lacking, the applicant shall be required to limit claims to overcome objection or may file divisional application(s). Applicants may also file divisionals voluntarily subject to national rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an applicant may proactively file a divisional, or must await an objection varies among AMS (exceptions: Myanmar and Thailand). Divisional subject-matter shall not go beyond the disclosure in the initial application. Divisional claims need not be limited to subject-matter already claimed in parent claims (to avoid double patenting issues applicants should consider national rules). Divisional application is deemed filed on the parent application's filing date and enjoys that application's priority. An application may give rise to more than one divisional; a divisional may itself give rise to further divisionals.
